build_profile: debug (unoptimized); ratios are meaningful, absolute times are not
method: in-process reconstruction on identical logs; `scan_audit_micros` is the pre-Phase-43 algorithm (whole-log header scan + newest valid checkpoint + replay tail); `catalogue_mount_cold` completes that scan once and publishes the derived committed-root directory, `catalogue_mount_warm` re-mounts using it and skips the whole-log discovery scan
note: Mount is NOT constant-time: with a checkpoint, replay is O(bytes after the checkpoint) and without one it is O(total history). Phase 43 removes the whole-log checkpoint *discovery* scan on a warm restart (a catalogue-complete directory lookup), but the checkpoint's embedded index must still be decoded, so the win grows with the retained log and can be a small loss when the scan was already cheap (the rows report both). `catalogue_mount_cold` additionally pays the one-time cost of publishing the directory (a few fsyncs). The log always wins: every catalogue checkpoint is re-read and re-validated.
